doc_description: Earnings release (Feb 8, 2023) for MGM Resorts International’s Q4 and full-year 2022 results highlighting record Adjusted Property EBITDAR at Las Vegas Strip and Regional operations, $2.8B of share repurchases with a new $2B authorization, the $1.1B sale of The Mirage operations, a renewed 10-year Macau gaming concession, and detailed non-GAAP reconciliations amid strong U.S. performance and weak MGM China.

structure.title: MGM RESORTS INTERNATIONAL REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FULL YEAR 2022 FINANCIAL AND OPERATING RESULTS
structure.heading: 1 MGM RESORTS INTERNATIONAL REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FULL YEAR 2022 FINANCIAL AND OPERATING RESULTS
structure.start_phrase: Las Vegas, Nevada, February 8, 2023 – MGM Resorts International (NYSE: MGM) (“MGM Resorts” or the “Company”) today reported financial results for the quarter and year ended December 31, 2022.
structure.summary:
- Exhibit 99.1: MGM Resorts International earnings release for Q4 and full year 2022 (dated Feb 8, 2023).
- Operational highlights: record Adjusted Property EBITDAR for Las Vegas Strip Resorts and Regional Operations in both Q4 and full year 2022.
- Capital returns: $2.8B share repurchases in 2022 (including $352M in Q4); Board approved an additional $2B buyback authorization. Cumulatively ~$4.7B repurchased since 2021; 4M shares ($164M) repurchased year-to-date in 2023.
- Strategic actions: closed sale of The Mirage operations for $1.1B in cash; awarded a new 10-year gaming concession in Macau.
- Executive commentary: CEO cites fifth consecutive record quarter for Las Vegas Strip Resorts EBITDAR, strong business momentum, and a positive 2023 outlook driven by events, MGM China’s rapid return to profitability YTD, and BetMGM’s improvement. CFO emphasizes free cash flow focus and compelling shareholder yield via continued buybacks.
- Q4 2022 financials: consolidated net revenues of $3.6B, up 18% year over year, benefiting from inclusion of The Cosmopolitan (acquired May 2022) and stronger volume/travel at Las Vegas Strip and Regional properties, partially offset by the Mirage disposition (Dec 2022).
- Profitability: operating loss of $2M vs. operating income of $369M in prior-year quarter, primarily due to a $1.2B increase in noncash amortization related to the MGM Grand Paradise gaming subconcession and a $338M increase in rent expense recorded within G&A tied to VICI and The Cosmopolitan.

nodes.title: Fourth Quarter 2022 Financial Highlights:
nodes.heading: 1.1 Fourth Quarter 2022 Financial Highlights:
nodes.start_phrase: Consolidated net revenues of $3.6 billion , an increase of 18% compared to the prior year quarter.
nodes.summary:
- MGM Resorts International reported Q4 and full-year 2022 financial and operating results, highlighting record Adjusted Property EBITDAR for both Las Vegas Strip Resorts and Regional Operations in Q4 and for the full year.
- Capital return: $2.8 billion of share repurchases in 2022, including $352 million in Q4; Board authorized a new $2 billion repurchase program. Year-to-date (early 2023), 4 million shares repurchased for $164 million; approximately $4.7 billion repurchased since 2021.
- Strategic transactions and milestones: closed the sale of The Mirage operations for $1.1 billion in cash; secured a new 10-year gaming concession in Macau.
- Management commentary: CEO cited a fifth consecutive quarter of record Las Vegas Strip Resorts Adjusted Property EBITDAR, strong business momentum, a robust 2023 events calendar, rapid return to profitability at MGM China year-to-date, and ongoing improvements at BetMGM. CFO emphasized focus on free cash flow, the company’s yield considering excess cash and ownership stakes in MGM China and BetMGM, and continued share repurchases.
- Q4 2022 consolidated financial highlights:
  - Net revenues of $3.6 billion, up 18% year over year, benefiting from inclusion of The Cosmopolitan (acquired May 2022) and improved travel and business volumes at Las Vegas Strip Resorts and Regional Operations, partially offset by the December 2022 disposition of The Mirage.
  - Operating loss of $2 million versus operating income of $369 million in the prior-year quarter, primarily due to a $1.2 billion increase in noncash amortization related to the MGM Grand Paradise gaming subconcession and a $338 million increase in rent expense recorded within G&A related to VICI and The Cosmopolitan.

nodes.title: Las Vegas Strip Resorts
nodes.heading: 1.1.2 Las Vegas Strip Resorts
nodes.start_phrase: Net r evenues of $2.3 billion in the current quarter compared to $1.8 billion in the prior year quarter, an increase of 27%.
nodes.summary:
- Consolidated results: Net income attributable to MGM Resorts was $284 million versus $131 million in the prior-year quarter; diluted EPS was $0.69 versus $0.23. Adjusted diluted EPS was a loss of $1.53 versus $0.12. Consolidated Adjusted EBITDAR was $957 million. Operating results were impacted by non-cash effects from leases that commenced in April and May 2022, partially offset by a $1.1 billion gain on the sale of The Mirage.

- Las Vegas Strip Resorts: Net revenues rose 27% to $2.3 billion, benefiting from the inclusion of The Cosmopolitan and stronger travel, partially offset by the Mirage disposition. Same-store net revenues increased 11% to $1.8 billion. Adjusted Property EBITDAR increased 26% to $877 million; same-store Adjusted Property EBITDAR rose 6% to $691 million. EBITDAR margin was 38.2% versus 38.7%, down 50 bps due to greater contribution from lower-margin non-gaming outlets and venues.

- Regional Operations: Net revenues increased 10% to $991 million on higher business volume. Adjusted Property EBITDAR grew 3% to $320 million. EBITDAR margin declined to 32.2% from 34.4% (down 215 bps) due to mix shift toward lower-margin non-gaming, higher G&A, and a prior-year $16 million insurance recovery (Hurricane Zeta).

- MGM China: Net revenues declined 44% to $175 million, impacted by a three-day COVID-19 closure at MGM Cotai and tighter Macau travel/entry restrictions versus the prior year. Adjusted Property EBITDAR was a loss of $55 million compared to $5 million of EBITDAR in the prior-year quarter.

License fee expense was $3 million (vs $6 million prior year).
- Unconsolidated affiliates: Company’s share of operating income (loss) showed a total loss of $40.3 million (vs $8.0 million loss prior year), with VICI BREIT Venture at $0 (vs $38.9 million), BetMGM at a $47.7 million loss (improved from $56.9 million loss), and Other at $7.3 million (vs $9.9 million).
- Shareholder returns: repurchased ~11 million shares in Q4 2022 at an average $32.96 for $352 million; $475 million remained under the March 2022 plan at year-end. nodes.title: About MGM Resorts International

nodes.start_phrase: MGM Resorts International (NYSE: MGM) is an S&P 500® global gaming and entertainment company with national and international locations featuring best -in-class hotels and casinos, state -of-the-art meetings and conference spaces, incredible live and theatrical entertainment experiences, and an extensive array of restaurant, nightlife and retail offerings.
nodes.summary:
- Corporate overview of MGM Resorts International: global gaming and entertainment footprint; portfolio of 32 hotel and gaming destinations; BetMGM 50/50 joint venture in North America; LeoVegas AB operations in Europe; targeted expansion in Japan; ESG focus (“Focused on What Matters”); recognition by FORTUNE; website and social media links.
- Forward-looking statements disclaimer: outlines expectations around transactions, balance sheet strength, free cash flow, liquidity, investment timing, strategy execution (Japan IR, BetMGM leadership), and shareholder returns; details key risks (COVID-19 impacts, economic/market conditions, competition, project design/timing/costs, international operations, permits/licenses/financing); references SEC filings; no obligation to update.
- Investor and media contacts: names, titles, phone numbers, and emails for Investment Community and News Media inquiries.
- Consolidated Statements of Operations (unaudited): quarterly and full-year comparisons for 2022 vs. 2021; revenue breakdown (casino, rooms, food & beverage, entertainment/retail/other, reimbursed costs); expense categories; notable items (property transactions, gains on REIT transactions, prior-year gain on CityCenter consolidation); operating and non-operating items; tax provision; net income and EPS; share counts.
- Consolidated Balance Sheets (unaudited): year-end 2022 vs. 2021; current assets (including cash and assets held for sale); property & equipment; other assets (goodwill, intangibles, operating lease ROU assets); liabilities (current, long-term debt, operating lease liabilities, deferred taxes); equity (retained earnings, AOCI, noncontrolling interests); note on restricted cash related to The Cosmopolitan acquisition.
- Segment supplemental data – Net revenues: breakdown by Las Vegas Strip Resorts, Regional Operations, MGM China, and Management/Other; shows strong Las Vegas and Regional performance and weaker MGM China.
- Segment supplemental data – Adjusted Property EBITDAR and total Adjusted EBITDAR: contributions by segment; impacts from unconsolidated affiliates, stock compensation, and corporate; footnotes clarifying treatment of real estate ventures and transaction/global development/MGM China-related corporate amounts.
- Reconciliation from Net Income to Adjusted EBITDAR: add-backs for taxes, interest, other non-operating items, preopening, property transactions, depreciation & amortization, triple-net and ground lease rent; adjustments for gains on REIT transactions and CityCenter consolidation; real estate venture impacts.
- Las Vegas Strip Resorts reconciliations: table games hold-adjusted net revenues and Adjusted Property EBITDAR, including definitions of hold adjustments and related expense impacts.
- Same-store reconciliations for Las Vegas Strip Resorts: adjustments excluding acquisitions (e.g., The Cosmopolitan, Aria) and dispositions (e.g., The Mirage); presentation of same-store net revenues and Adjusted Property EBITDAR with hold adjustments.
- Overall, the section constitutes the back matter of an earnings release: company overview and legal disclaimers, investor/media contacts, detailed unaudited financial statements, segment results, and non-GAAP reconciliations.
